title: We locked 25,396 behaviors before our agent refactors its own code, bugs included
content: Before letting our Claude Code agent restructure its own codebase, we had it write 25,396 tests in 769 files that pin what the code does today, bugs included, each one running in a sandbox with no writes into the repo, no network and no secrets. So far six commits have had to change a pinned expectation and say why, three bugs came out of the work of writing the cases, and one full run took 8 minutes 44 seconds on a heavily loaded 10-core machine. What we were protecting Our agent maintains its own TypeScript codebase: the scripts behind its daily jobs, about 230 command-line tools under src/commands , the checks that run before every commit, and the JSONL ledgers it reads to decide what to do next. On 2026-10-08 the owner asked for tests that would hold every current behavior in place through a very large refactor, a move toward a domain-driven layout. title: A Cost-Aware Model Router for Claude in About 80 Lines of Python
content: The fastest way to cut an LLM bill without hurting quality is to stop sending every request to your most capable model. Most traffic in a typical agent workflow is classification, extraction, or short replies. A smaller, faster model handles those fine. The bigger model should be reserved for the steps where it measurably changes the outcome. This post walks through the simple router I use with Claude models. It's not a framework. It's a pattern you can adapt in an afternoon. The idea Every request gets a cheap first pass that decides how hard it is. Easy requests go to a fast model. Hard ones go to a stronger model. If the fast model's answer fails a check, the request is retried on the stronger one. Three ingredients: A difficulty signal : rules, a small classifier, or a short call to the fast model itself. title: Agentes LLM: un cortocircuito para email
content: Cuando un agente LLM puede crear una cuenta, solicitar un código y leer un mensaje, una falla de email no debería provocar diez reintentos iguales. En sistemas de automatización, insistir no es lo mismo que recuperarse. La idea de este diseño es sencilla: envolver la herramienta de email en un cortocircuito . Si el proveedor está lento, el inbox no pertenece a la ejecución o el mismo mensaje ya fue procesado, la herramienta debe pasar a un estado limitado y explicarle al agente qué hacer despues. Esto es especialmente útil cuando se trabaja con un use and throw email para pruebas. El buzón puede ser temporal, pero las decisiones del agente deben ser trazables. El problema: un agente puede insistir demasiado Un flujo típico se ve así: El agente crea un usuario de prueba. Solicita un email de confirmación. Consulta el inbox cada pocos segundos. Si no encuentra nada, repite la consulta o vuelve a enviar el mensaje. El cuarto paso parece razonable hasta que se combinan varias ejecuciones.

title: 11 Prompt Engineering Practices That Survive Production
content: This is a condensed version of our full guide. The original, with diagrams, evaluation methods and a section on enterprise prompt architecture, is on our blog: Prompt Engineering Guide 2026 . Most prompt advice is written for chat: how to get a nicer answer from a chatbot once. Production is different. A prompt in a product runs thousands of times a day, on inputs nobody has seen, and its output is often parsed by code rather than read by a person. A clever one-off trick does not survive that. A disciplined habit does. These are the eleven practices that most reliably separate production-grade prompting from trial and error in the systems we build. None of them depend on a particular model or provider. 1. Be specific and unambiguous Vague instructions produce vague results. "Summarise this ticket" leaves the model to guess the length, audience and focus. "Summarise this support ticket in two sentences for an on-call engineer: what broke and what the customer already tried" does not. Pr

title: fix(install): treat .pi as a foreign platform path (#3560)
content:
fix(install): treat .pi as a foreign platform path (#3560)

The platform-configs module lists `.pi`, but PLATFORM_SOURCE_PATH_OWNERS
had no entry for it, so isForeignPlatformPath() returned false and every
install-apply target (e.g. `--target opencode`) copied the Pi harness
adapter (.pi/README.md, .pi/extensions/*) into its config root and
recorded it as ECC-managed.

Pi consumes ECC through `pi install`, not install-apply, so map `.pi` to
the `pi` owner. No install target has that id, so the directory is now
filtered out everywhere, like `.codex`, `.cursor`, and `.zed`.

Add regression tests for the opencode plan and for every registered
target.

Fixes #3558

title: test(runner): add a worker pool and an ECC_TEST_ONLY filter to run-all
content:
test(runner): add a worker pool and an ECC_TEST_ONLY filter to run-all

The runner executed 422 files one process at a time, which is most of
the 12 to 40 minutes a CI lane spends in "Run tests". ECC_TEST_JOBS
above 1 now runs files through a pool of that many processes; output is
still buffered and printed per file, so logs read the same. The default
stays 1 and that path is the original synchronous spawnSync loop, so the
VM-driven runner test and the piped-output tests are unchanged.

ECC_TEST_ONLY is the mirror of ECC_TEST_SKIP: a comma-separated list of
path substrings, and only matching files run. CI uses it to give the
package-manager lanes just the suites that read the package-manager
variable instead of the whole suite.

Two real-process tests cover the pool (grouped output, counted failure,
summary last) and the ONLY filter.

title: Every TheKitBase Template Ships AI-Ready: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and .cursorrules
content: Open an unfamiliar codebase in a coding agent and the first few prompts are rarely about the feature you actually want. They're spent on reconnaissance: where does the data live, what's the token system called, is this a server component by default, which file would a human on this team touch to add a page. A generic template leaves the agent to guess at all of it, and a wrong guess costs you a revert. What ships in every template CLAUDE.md - read by Claude Code on open. Commands, routes, where things live, the design-token system, conventions, how to add a page, and what not to touch. AGENTS.md - the same instructions in the shared format a growing list of agents read, OpenAI Codex among them. .cursorrules - the same instructions again, as the rules file Cursor loads for the project. All three carry identical content. They're generated from one shared structure per template, so the conventions stay consistent across the whole catalog rather than drifting from one template to the next
author: TheKitBase
summary_zh: 文章介绍 TheKitBase 的每个模板都自带 CLAUDE.md、AGENTS.md 和 .cursorrules 三类 AI 指令文件。这些文件写明了命令、路由、代码位置、设计令牌系统、团队约定、如何新增页面以及哪些部分不要改动，这样 AI 编程代理打开陌生代码库时不必反复摸索，也能减少猜错带来的回滚。这一做法可以作为跨 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 统一维护项目上下文的参考，但文章带有明显的产品推广性质。

title: Running Claude Code with Ollama and Local Models
content: Claude Code + Ollama: Coding with a Local Model Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool. It reads your project, edits files, and runs commands from the terminal. With Ollama , you can run it on a model hosted on your own machine instead of in the cloud. Why local models? Your code never leaves your machine No API costs Works offline In this guide, you'll install Claude Code, run it inside IntelliJ IDEA, connect it to Ollama, and test it on a small Java project. Step 1: Install Claude Code Install it globally with npm: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code Then open a terminal and run: claude
author: SEBAA Mohammed
summary_zh: 这是一篇入门教程，介绍如何把 Claude Code 接到 Ollama 上，改用本机运行的模型，好处是代码不离开本机、不产生 API 费用、也能离线使用。文章按顺序讲了安装 Claude Code、在 IntelliJ IDEA 里运行、连接 Ollama，并用一个小型 Java 项目做测试。目前给出的内容只到安装这一步，信息密度有限。
